problem: Zero-shot VLN-CE methods depend on depth sensors, LiDAR, panoramic cameras or odometry, and use separate visual features for geometric mapping and semantic navigation. This causes spatial-semantic inconsistency, coarse value maps, and weak control over long-horizon failures.
motivation: Monocular RGB-only navigation lowers hardware cost and calibration complexity for real robots. Semantic value maps built from image-level language similarity are coarse and drift across viewpoints. Long-horizon episodes need an explicit, inspectable state to track sub-instructions and recover from false detections, unreachable subgoals and planning failures.
key_idea: Share dense CleanDIFT diffusion features between VGGT-based monocular geometry (correspondence filtering) and semantic value-map construction (visual-reference similarity fused with BLIP-2 relevance), and orchestrate perception, planning and recovery as a LangGraph state machine.
insight: The value-map ablation shows the two semantic signals are complementary: removing CleanDIFT drops SR from 21.3 to 3.0, and removing BLIP-2 drops it to 12.0. The geometry ablation shows online estimation costs little: with GT depth and GT pose SR is 24.9 vs 21.3 for fully predicted, and replacing GT pose with predicted pose hurts NE more (0.81 m) than replacing GT depth (0.24 m). Depth error is mostly a per-frame scale issue (AbsRel 0.5874 with fixed s0 vs 0.0493 with per-frame median alignment), and semantic filtering reduces RTE from 0.150 to 0.092 m.
method: Stateful LangGraph orchestration: shared persistent state (sub-instruction, pose, map, history) with initialization, normal navigation, recovery and termination branches, and conditional transitions.
Monocular metric reconstruction: VGGT predicts depth, point maps and confidence. Scale s0 is the median of h_cam/|b| from ground-plane fits over a 12-heading panoramic scan.
Semantic outlier rejection: CleanDIFT cosine similarity filters inter-frame correspondences (tau_sem 0.65). Weighted RANSAC plus robust refinement gives a bounded Sim(3) registration.

Constraint tracking: an LLM and rules decompose the instruction into sub-instructions with object (Grounding DINO + SAM2), location (BLIP VQA/ITM with a state machine) and direction (turn vs displacement) constraints.

Semantic value map: fuses the CleanDIFT reference-similarity map A and the BLIP-2 relevance map B with confidence weights. Values are temporally reprojected and accumulated in a global BEV map with traversability, occupancy and feature layers.

Waypoint selection and planning: semantics-augmented SLIC regions in the reachable area, region-mean scoring, hysteresis and loop suppression. FMM gives the short-term goal, executed as Forward 0.25 m / Turn 30°.

Three-level recovery: viewpoint recovery (panoramic re-look), semantic recovery (refresh grounding), navigation redirection (frontier exploration), triggered by a stagnation counter, with at most 3 attempts.

setting.backbone: Frozen foundation models: VGGT, CleanDIFT, BLIP-2, Grounding DINO, SAM2, a lightweight LLM for instruction parsing
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB only (known camera height, initial 360° panoramic scan by rotating in place)
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN LEFT/RIGHT 30° / STOP
setting.privileged: none at test time; known camera mounting height h_cam; the initial panoramic scan is excluded from the 150-action budget

numbers.eval_set_note: 550 episodes (50 from each of the 11 unseen scenes); baselines re-run on the same subset; 150 low-level action budget; 3.0 m success threshold
numbers.backbone: VGGT + CleanDIFT + BLIP-2 + Grounding DINO/SAM2 + LLM (frozen)
numbers.extra: monocular RGB only, known camera height, initial panoramic scan excluded from action budget
numbers.evidence: Table 1 main zero-shot VLN-CE results on a fixed 550-episode subset of R2R-CE val-unseen

numbers.extra: uses Habitat GT depth and pose

results: On a 550-episode R2R-CE val-unseen subset, monocular-RGB LG-VLN reaches SR 21.3 / SPL 12.1 / OSR 29.5 / NE 7.85. This is close to CA-Nav's SR of 22.4 (RGB-D + odometry) and above InstructNav's 15.1 (GT pose). It beats CA-Nav on SPL (12.1 vs 9.3) but trails on OSR (29.5 vs 43.7). NavGPT (31.8 SR) and Open-Nav (26.4 SR) score higher on SR, but NavGPT plans on a discrete nav-graph and Open-Nav uses panoramic RGB-D and a trained waypoint predictor.
limitations: Evaluated only on a 550-episode subset in a single run, so SR differences are within noise; no full-split or real-robot results.

Depends on a known camera height and an initial 360° scan for scale, and uses a single global scale, so fixed-scale depth AbsRel is high (mean 0.5874); it also has a low OSR because of conservative exploration.
Heavy pipeline: many foundation models, with Grounding DINO + SAM2 taking about 602 ms per call and VGGT and CleanDIFT about 178 and 179 ms per frame.
